methods_en: EPA NFA evaluation used 194 chemicals from original folds 1–4; fold 0 contained 49 development chemicals. Both arms used three measured concentrations and the same five published test contexts, features and 600 absolute-error boosting iterations. The five-design arm physically repeated valid training rows within each chemical to match exactly the full-enumeration scalar-row count; the remainder used a chemical-seeded permutation. Both arms were run in the identical Python, NumPy, scikit-learn and single-thread environment; the historical full-enumeration run was retained separately. Chemical-averaged curve MAE differences were bootstrapped 10,000 times with seed 0. The matched budget is scalar rows times boosting iterations; wall-clock time and unique design coverage are separately reported.
results_en: Full enumeration yielded 1.94% lower curve MAE than five-design training with matched row and iteration budgets (1.160612 versus 1.183515; delta -0.022903, 95% chemical-bootstrap interval [-0.035089, -0.012074]; n=194). Chemical wins/losses/ties were 134/60/0; fold wins/losses/ties were 4/0/0.

anchor_control.methods_en: The second control reused all four original frozen evaluation folds and the full-enumeration 600-iteration training budget. Direct-target boosting retained the interpolation-anchor input features but omitted residual-target subtraction and anchor addition. Both historical arms used identical training rows and 22 features. The paired 95% interval used 10,000 chemical bootstrap replicates with seed 0.
anchor_control.results_en: Residual-target boosting had curve MAE 1.160612 versus 1.169185 for direct-target boosting (delta -0.008573, 95% interval [-0.033706, +0.006656]; n=194). Chemical wins/losses/ties were 97/97/0.
